title: Casebook: Detective and Investigation Sound Effects
shortText: 124 detective and mystery SFX: evidence by kind, corkboard, deduction, interrogation, accusation. WAV + OGG.
html:
The whole investigation, as one sound

124 sound effects for detective, mystery and investigation games: examine, evidence sorted by kind, the corkboard, the deduction, the interrogation and the accusation, in one paper, brass and rain sound.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No attribution required. Use it in as many games as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the sounds themselves as a sound pack. The plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy and paste credit line for anyone who wants one. Everything is synthesised from code, so there is no upstream sample licence behind it.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 32 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. The whole evidence grid (all 8 kinds, found and logged), the whole certainty ladder, the interrogation room at its lowest and highest tier, the tape recorder in every state, the office at night, a link confirmed on the board, the contradiction strike and the case closed stamp.

Evidence, sorted by kind

A detective game logs evidence all the time, and every clue sounding the same is the first thing a player notices. Here each kind sounds like itself twice: when the player finds it, and when it goes into the casebook.

  • Key: a steel key found on the floor, then dropped into an evidence bag and sealed.
  • Shell casing: a brass casing that rolls to a stop, then tipped into a small envelope.
  • Fibre: a thread lifted on tweezers, then folded into a paper envelope and stapled.
  • Photograph: a glossy print slid out of a sleeve, then clipped into the casebook.
  • Document: a folded letter opened out, then filed into a folder under a paper clip.
  • Audio tape: a cassette knocked out of a drawer, then snapped shut in its case.
  • Fingerprint: powder brushed across a surface, then the print lifted on tape and pressed onto a card.
  • Stain: an ultraviolet lamp hums on over a stain, then a swab goes into a capped tube.

Checked from the shipped files, not promised: across the kind by stage grid the kind changes the sound and so does the stage (64 pairs, 0 alike). Wiring it is one string: evidence_key_found, evidence_key_logged.

Meters you can hear

4 ladders a game can index by number:

  • Certainty, 5 levels: a brass latch at five levels of certainty, each one brighter and more sure than the last, so a game can voice a deduction meter.
  • Interrogation pressure, 5 levels: a hand on the interrogation table at five levels of pressure, from two fingertip taps to a slam that rattles the cup, each rung longer than the last.
  • The room, by tension, 5 levels: the interrogation room itself at five tiers of tension, a seamless loop per tier: the clock and the tube light, then the rain on the window, the fidgeting, and at the top a thin whine, each tier brighter than the last.
  • Credibility lost, 3 levels: a mark struck off the record once, twice and three times, for a wrong accusation that costs credibility.

Measured from the shipped files: 14 steps, every brightness step at least 8% and every length step at least 12%, failing steps: 0.

The detective's kit

9 tools, every state of each: the tape recorder (record, play, stop, rewind, eject); the rotary phone (ring, pick up, dial, hang up); the flashlight (on, off, flicker); the ultraviolet lamp (on, hum, off); the camera (shutter, flash charge, flash pop); the desk lamp (on, off); the case file (open, close); the interview room door (open, close, lock); the magnifier (raise, lower). No two states of one tool are the same sound renamed (31 pairs measured, 0 alike), and the phone's ring and the lamp's hum are seamless loops.

The rest of the case

  • 11 examine sounds: a magnifier raised and lowered, three hotspot hovers, nothing here, something here, zoom in and out, an object turned over and a lens focus.
  • 11 corkboard sounds: pins pushed and pulled, photos and cards pinned, the red string stretched, a link confirmed, a link rejected and the board cleared.
  • 11 deduction sounds: the certainty ladder, a deduction locked in, a theory complete, a theory falling apart, a thought connected, a thought discarded and a moment of doubt.
  • 22 interrogation sounds: the pressure ladder, five tiers of the room as loops, a statement logged and pressed, evidence presented, a lie caught, the contradiction strike, a witness breaking, chairs, a cup and the interview room door.
  • 8 accusation sounds: the accusation, the case closed stamp, a wrong accusation, credibility lost three ways, a case reopened and a confession signed.
  • 7 case file and scene sounds and 6 interface sounds: the file opened and closed, a chapter card in and out, soft and hard scene cuts, a folder slid across the desk; hover, select, back, a tab, an error and notes saved.
  • 5 places, as loops: the office at night with rain on the window, the precinct, a crime scene apartment, the records archive and a stakeout in a parked car.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a naming manifest listing every file by group.
  • 12 seamless loops of 3.0 to 6.0 seconds with loop points in both formats, and none on a one shot.
  • One office, one cell: every one shot sits in the same small wood panelled room, and the interrogation group in the bare cell down the corridor, so the pack sounds like one building.
  • 6 variation sets whose takes differ in length and in brightness.
  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 0.93 dB, so a palm on the table and a menu tick share a mix.
  • Import notes for Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker, Ren'Py and the web, and pack_proof.json with a sha256 and a measurement for every file: 1139 checks, 0 failed.

Already own our other sound packs?

Every file here was measured against every file in the studio's 5 nearest packs (stealth, typewriters, horror, urban place beds and weather: 68696 pairs, on spectral shape and on envelope, each tolerant of a transposition): 68696 of 68696 are separate sounds. The proof ships in the download as cross_pack_proof.json.

Honest limits

These are synthesised sounds designed for games, not field recordings: paper, card and cork, brass, steel, bakelite, glass and rain heard through a window. The figures above are signal measurements, not a claim that anything sounds good; that is what the free demo is for. There are no voices and no music: a deduction lands as a brass latch and a case closes with a rubber stamp, never a sting.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis by Core Systems Asset Factory, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover and the store graphics are drawn by AI written code from the pack's own waveforms.

More from the same studio

  • Verdict Core, an investigation, cross examination and deduction system for RPG Maker MV and MZ.
  • Dossier for GameMaker and Dossier for Unity, the same case file and deduction idea for those engines.
  • Unseen, stealth sound effects for when the detective goes somewhere they should not be.
  • Typeset, typewriter and handwriting text sounds for the case notes on screen.
